c.tagline: Harbour city of sails, volcanoes and endless coastline.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares vary by company; agree on a fixed price for airport transfers or use SkyBus/rideshare instead.

emergency.note: 111 is the single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance nationwide; Auckland City Hospital operates the main public emergency department.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for late-night rowdiness on lower Queen Street and Karangahape Road, and never leave valuables in parked cars at beaches or trailheads.

hood_desc: The commercial and entertainment core with Sky Tower, Queen Street shopping, waterfront ferries, and Britomart's dining precinct; suits first-timers who want everything walkable and no transport hassle.
Waterfront marina district with superyachts, upscale seafood restaurants, and easy walk to Sky Tower and the Ferry Building; suits couples and business travelers wanting a scenic, polished base.
Auckland's trendiest strip of villas, boutiques, cafes and bars along Ponsonby Road; suits foodies, younger travelers and anyone wanting a distinct neighborhood vibe just outside the CBD.
Leafy, historic garden suburb with boutique shops, Auckland Domain and the Museum nearby; suits couples and travelers wanting a quieter, upscale base a short bus or walk from downtown.
A charming harbourside village reached by a scenic 12-minute ferry ride, with beaches, cafes and Victorian villas; suits travelers wanting a relaxed, low-key stay with easy CBD access by boat.

water.note: Tap water is treated to high standards and safe to drink straight from the tap.

sys.n: Auckland Metro (electric train network: Southern, Western, Eastern, Onehunga lines)
AT Metro Bus (including City Link, Inner Link, Outer Link)
Auckland Ferry (to Devonport, Waiheke Island, Half Moon Bay etc.)
Northern Busway (dedicated bus rapid transit corridor)

transit.pay: Visitors tap on/off with an AT HOP card (available from stations, retailers or the AT Metro app) loaded with cash; contactless bank card and Apple/Google Pay tap-and-go is also accepted on trains, most buses and ferries. Single paper tickets are not available on trains.
transit.hours: Trains and buses run roughly 5am-midnight on weekdays with reduced late-night and Sunday frequency; there is no true 24-hour service, so night owls rely on taxis or rideshare after midnight.
transit.note: The City Rail Link (a new underground rail tunnel through downtown) has been under construction and is progressively opening, improving cross-city train frequency.

train: Auckland Metro suburban rail (Southern, Western, Eastern, Onehunga lines)
Northern Explorer long-distance train to Wellington
bus: AT Metro city and regional buses
ferry: Fullers360 ferries to Devonport, Waiheke Island, Rangitoto and other Hauraki Gulf destinations

transit.m: SkyBus Airport Express (bus, ~45-60 min to CBD)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in New Zealand; a small tip for exceptional service is appreciated but never expected, and service charges are rarely added.

food.name: Hangi
food.desc: Maori earth-oven cooking: meat, kumara and vegetables steamed for hours over hot stones under the ground, giving everything a smoky sweetness.

places.name: Otara Flea Market
places.note: Saturday-morning market where hangi packs sell out early alongside Pacific stalls.

places.name: Avondale Sunday Market
places.note: Sprawling Sunday market with hangi, boil-up and fresh island produce.

places.name: Auckland Night Markets
places.note: Rotating weeknight markets where hangi and steamed pudding stalls appear.

food.name: Whitebait fritter
food.desc: A New Zealand delicacy: tiny translucent whitebait bound with egg, fried into a thin fritter and served with lemon and white bread.

places.name: Depot Eatery
places.note: Al Brown's shared-plate bistro; whitebait appears when the season is running.

places.name: Ahi
places.note: Ben Bayly's Michelin-starred NZ produce restaurant; whitebait when the season runs.

places.name: The Oyster Inn
places.note: Island bistro worth the ferry for fritters, oysters and a glass of local white.

food.name: Fish and chips
food.desc: Battered snapper, hoki or gurnard with chips, wrapped in paper and eaten on the beach - the standard Kiwi Friday night.

places.name: Fish Smith
places.note: Modern chippie using sustainable NZ fish and beef-dripping chips.

places.name: Auckland Fish Market
places.note: Buy straight from the fishmongers or eat fried-to-order by the water.

food.name: Pacific Island fare
food.desc: Auckland is the largest Polynesian city on earth. Look for palusami, taro, chop suey and umu-cooked pork across the southern suburbs.

places.name: Mangere Town Centre
places.note: Takeaways and bakeries serving Samoan and Tongan plates all day.

places.name: Otahuhu shops
places.note: Island grocers and hot-food counters for taro, lu sipi and coconut buns.

places.name: Otara Flea Market
places.note: Saturday market with the best concentration of Pacific food stalls in the city.

food.name: Green-lipped mussels
food.desc: New Zealand's big emerald-shelled mussels, farmed in the Coromandel and Marlborough and usually steamed with wine, chilli and coconut.

places.name: Kingi
places.note: Britomart seafood bistro serving Mills Bay green-lipped mussels and NZ shellfish.

places.name: Soul Bar & Bistro
places.note: Long-running harbourside bistro; seafood plates and people-watching.

places.name: Auckland Fish Market
places.note: Buy them live from the fishmonger or eat them cooked at the market bars.

food.name: Hokey pokey ice cream
food.desc: New Zealand's national ice cream: vanilla studded with shards of honeycomb toffee, invented here and sold in every dairy and gelato shop.

places.name: Giapo
places.note: Theatrical ice cream lab building sculptural cones to order.

places.name: Duck Island Ice Cream
places.note: Cult NZ scoop shop with hokey pokey alongside wild rotating flavours.

places.name: Island Gelato Company
places.note: Waiheke-born gelato using NZ milk, with a honeycomb version in the case.

food.name: L&P (Lemon & Paeroa)
food.desc: World famous in New Zealand: a lemony mineral-water soda first bottled in the town of Paeroa, and the standard partner to fish and chips.

places.name: Fish Smith
places.note: Cold bottles in the fridge to drink with the fish and chips.

places.name: Otara Flea Market
places.note: Market stalls sell it icy cold beside the hangi and island food.

places.name: Corner dairies
places.note: Any neighbourhood dairy stocks it; the glass bottle is the way to go.

food.name: New Zealand craft beer
food.desc: NZ hops like Nelson Sauvin and Motueka give local pale ales and IPAs a distinctive tropical, gooseberry note. Auckland has taprooms citywide.

places.name: Galbraith's Alehouse
places.note: Historic pub brewing real ales on site since 1995.

places.name: Urbanaut Brewing Co
places.note: Playful taproom known for hazy and mixed-flavour small batches.

places.name: Brothers Beer
places.note: Central warehouse bar with dozens of NZ taps and a big bottle wall.

landmarks: Sky Tower
New Zealand's tallest structure dominates the skyline and offers panoramic city and harbor views from its observation decks.
Auckland Harbour Bridge
This elegant steel bridge spanning the Waitematā Harbour is a defining image of Auckland's cityscape, especially at sunset.
One Tree Hill (Maungakiekie)
A volcanic cone crowned by an obelisk and surrounded by Cornwall Park's rolling farmland, offering sweeping 360-degree views of the city.
Auckland War Memorial Museum
A grand neoclassical building perched atop the Domain, housing world-class Māori and Pacific taonga and serving as a proud civic landmark.
Mount Eden (Maungawhau)
Auckland's highest volcanic cone features a dramatic grassy crater and unbeatable panoramic views of the entire isthmus.
Rangitoto Island
This iconic symmetrical volcanic island silhouette anchors nearly every Auckland harbor photograph and is a popular day-trip hike.
Viaduct Harbour
A buzzing waterfront precinct of superyachts, bars, and restaurants that captures Auckland's title as the 'City of Sails.'
North Head, Devonport
A historic volcanic headland riddled with old gun emplacements and tunnels, offering some of the best skyline views across the harbor.
Auckland Domain & Wintergardens
Historic Victorian glasshouses filled with exotic and tropical plants sit within Auckland's oldest and largest park.
Piha Beach & Lion Rock
A wild black-sand surf beach on Auckland's west coast, dominated by the striking volcanic sea stack of Lion Rock, beloved by photographers.

train.note: New Zealand is an island nation with no international trains. Long-distance trains leave from Auckland Strand: KiwiRail's Great Journeys 'Northern Explorer' runs the scenic route to Wellington a few days a week. Separately, the Te Huia commuter train (https://www.tehuiatrain.co.nz/) links The Strand with Hamilton on weekdays.

bus.note: No international coaches. InterCity (https://www.intercity.co.nz/) is New Zealand's main long-distance bus network, running from central Auckland to destinations across the North Island and, via the ferry, the South Island.

ferry.note: No international passenger ferries. New Zealand's inter-island Interislander (https://www.interislander.co.nz/) sails Wellington-Picton, not from Auckland. Auckland's own ferries (Fullers360, https://www.fullers.co.nz/) are local harbour services to Devonport, Waiheke and other Hauraki Gulf islands.
